newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - China continues to spook market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - China continues to spook market.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil market continued to be haunted by China's long buying absence with traders now placing the near term support at $19.50 per barrel, traders said on Thursday.
"Let's look at $19.50 first before talking about $19.00 (as the next support)," a trader said.
China's continued absence due to a large supply overhang on the mainland, is the main reason for buyers' unwillingness to commit themselves.
Traders now said China would continue to abstain from buying on the open market or to drastically reduce its imports until the end of the year, which worsened the pall hanging over the market.
They said no refineries in Singapore could be said to be running at full capacity at the moment despite only two refineries actually known to have cut throughput.
Nevertheless, middle-distillate stocks continued to build after last week's fall. For the week ended July 9, Singapore stocks rose by 720,000 barrels to 11.464 million.
They said stocks continued to rise despite the reduced refinery runs because refiners have not been able to sell off their supplies.

On Thursday, a major offered slightly higher at $19.99 per barrel for second-half July lifting, free-on-board basis from Wednesday's $148 per tonne ($19.80 per barrel). The highest offer was made by a Dutch trader at $20.25 per barrel.
Jet fuel dipped to be offered at $21.75 from Wednesday's deal at $22.10.
Traders said India was expected to reissue its eight-month term tender to import gas oil and kerosene, which it cancelled late last week.
